market_summary: Markets are being whipsawed by an idiosyncratic shock at Nvidia (board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid affair allegations, stock -9% after hours on Nov 11), which is dragging on tech/semis sentiment just days before Nvidia's own earnings (Nov 17). In Singapore, bank earnings diverged sharply - OCBC beat Q3 estimates while DBS and UOB missed on weaker trading income and margin pressure, and both remain in technical downtrends (below 50/200-day averages). Singapore Airlines posted a 44% profit decline on surging jet fuel costs tied to Middle East conflict, yet the stock has still rallied 9% over the past month, leaving it stretched relative to depressed earnings. Apple continues to benefit from a strong Q4 beat and fresh analyst upgrades, holding near 52-week highs. Overall, dispersion is high: idiosyncratic single-stock risk (NVDA, SIA) matters more right now than broad index direction.

picks.thesis: Governance crisis (potential CEO removal) is a fresh, material negative catalyst layered on top of an already-weak technical picture (down 23% in a month, 20% below its 50-day average, relative volume 3x normal). Even if Huang stays, the uncertainty itself is bearish into the Nov 17 earnings date, and sell-side is already starting to trim targets (Baird cut target 500→200 on Nov 11).
picks.news: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang over affairs including one involving a suspected Chinese spy; shares fell >9% after hours (CNBC, 2026-11-11). Baird downgraded Outperform→Neutral, target 500→200 same day.
picks.risks: If the board denies/clarifies the story quickly or Huang is retained, the stock could snap back hard given how beaten down it already is (57 of 62 analysts still rate it Buy with huge implied upside). Earnings on Nov 17 could also surprise positively and overwhelm the governance headline.

picks.thesis: SIA's H1 net profit fell 44% on an 87% YoY jump in jet fuel costs from Middle East conflict escalation, yet the stock has rallied 9.3% over the past month and trades above its consensus analyst target (implied upside is actually negative, -2.3%), with only 1 of 13 analysts rating it Buy. The disconnect between deteriorating fundamentals and a resilient share price looks unsustainable if fuel costs stay elevated.
picks.news: SIA Group H1 FY2026/27 net profit fell 43.9% to S$134m despite record S$11.3b revenue, driven by an 86.7% YoY jump in jet fuel prices tied to West Asia conflict (Malay Mail, 2026-11-11).
picks.risks: A ceasefire or de-escalation in the Middle East could quickly ease fuel costs and remove the main earnings drag; strong travel demand/record revenue could also keep sentiment positive regardless of margins.

picks.thesis: UOB is the weakest of the three Singapore banks technically (down 7.2% over 1 month, 9.2% below its 50-day average and 5% below its 200-day average) and sentiment is the most negative of the group (9 of 16 analysts at Hold, only 5 Buy). While UOB itself hasn't reported yet this cycle in the news feed, the read-through from DBS's Q3 miss (trading income down 65% on volatile equity markets) suggests sector-wide margin/trading headwinds that likely also pressure UOB.
picks.news: DBS Q3 net profit fell 5% to S$2.81b, missing estimates, as markets trading income fell 65% amid volatile equity conditions (Bloomberg, 2026-11-05); OCBC was the only SG bank to beat Q3 estimates (Time, 2026-11-06), implying UOB/DBS faced a tougher backdrop.
picks.risks: This is an indirect, sector read-through rather than UOB-specific news, so there's a real chance UOB's own results differ; a rebound in regional equity trading volumes or lower-for-longer narrative on rates could lift all SG banks together.

picks.thesis: OCBC was the only one of the three Singapore banks to beat Q3 estimates, with record banking operating profit on strong loan growth and trading income - the opposite of the margin/trading pressure that hit DBS and UOB. This relative earnings resilience should support OCBC outperforming its SG bank peers even as the whole sector sits below its 52-week highs.
picks.news: OCBC posted Q3 net profit of S$2.04b, up 3% YoY, beating the S$2.00b consensus, with record banking profit of S$1.90b (Time, 2026-11-06).
picks.risks: OCBC is still down ~9% from its 52-week high and trades below its 50-day average, so broader SG bank sector weakness (rate cuts, equity market volatility) could still drag it down regardless of its relative earnings strength.

picks.thesis: Apple posted a solid fiscal Q4 beat (revenue +12% YoY, EPS beat) with record iPhone and Services revenue, and just received a fresh analyst upgrade (China Renaissance Hold→Buy, target 425). The stock is near its 52-week high and well above its 50- and 200-day averages, showing a durable uptrend that contrasts with the volatility hitting other mega-cap tech names (NVDA, GOOGL, META) this week.
picks.news: Apple Q4 FY2026 revenue $114.5b (+12% YoY), EPS $2.10 beat $1.99 consensus, record iPhone and Services revenue (SEC 8-K, 2026-11-02); China Renaissance upgraded to Buy on 2026-11-11.
picks.risks: Apple's own consensus price target (344.6) is now slightly below the current price, meaning further upside may be limited near-term, and any broad tech-sector selloff triggered by the NVDA governance scandal could still drag Apple down with it despite its relative strength.

picks.thesis: The Nasdaq-100 is heavily weighted toward mega-cap tech including Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta, several of which are showing fresh weakness (NVDA governance scandal, MSFT -4.4% in a day, GOOGL down 17% over a month). QQQ is already 9% below its 52-week high and below both its 50- and 200-day averages, and incremental bad news from any single mega-cap can disproportionately weigh on the index over the next few trading sessions, especially heading into Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings.
picks.news: Nvidia board turmoil reported Nov 11 (CNBC); Microsoft shares fell 4.4% same session per price data, reflecting broad mega-cap tech weakness.
picks.risks: This is a low-conviction, short-horizon tactical view based on sector composition rather than QQQ-specific news; a quick resolution of the Nvidia situation or strong earnings from other components could reverse the index quickly, and QQQ is a diversified basket that can absorb single-stock shocks.
